title: NASA astronaut and 2 cosmonauts blast off for an 8-month stay in space
facts: NASA astronaut Anil Menon launched to space alongside Russian cosmonauts Pyotr Dubrov and Anna Kikina aboard Soyuz MS-29.
The Soyuz MS-29 mission launched from the Baikonur Cosmodrome in Kazakhstan at 10:47 a.m. EDT on July 14, 2026.
Soyuz MS-29 docked with the International Space Station's Prichal module at 1:52 p.m. EDT.
The crew of Soyuz MS-29 is scheduled to remain aboard the International Space Station for an eight-month stay of roughly 260 days.
Anil Menon previously worked as a flight surgeon for NASA and SpaceX before being selected for NASA's astronaut corps in 2021.
Anna Menon, wife of Anil Menon, was selected to join NASA's astronaut corps in 2025.
Anna Menon previously flew to space in 2024 on a five-day commercial Crew Dragon mission chartered by Jared Isaacman.
Jared Isaacman serves as the Administrator of NASA.
Soyuz MS-29 docked with the space station while flying 260 miles above the Mediterranean Sea.
Soyuz MS-28 commander Sergey Kud-Sverchkov welcomed the incoming crew aboard the space station.
NASA astronaut Chris Williams was among the crew members already aboard the International Space Station.
The incoming Soyuz MS-29 crew is replacing the crew members of Soyuz MS-28 who arrived in November 2025.
Russian space authorities extended station missions from six months to eight months to reduce cargo shipment requirements.
The bilateral flight agreement between NASA and Roscosmos requires at least one US astronaut per Soyuz flight and one cosmonaut per SpaceX Crew Dragon flight.
Cosmonaut Anna Kikina previously completed her first spaceflight aboard a SpaceX Crew Dragon in 2022.
